summary:
"Abandoned But Not Forgotten - Luminary-NASA-21694" is a cinematic storytelling website about the machines we left behind. Ten NASA missions, five on the Moon and five on Mars, each get their own chapter: Eagle, Surveyor 3, the Apollo rovers, Charlie Duke’s family photo, Viking 1, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Ingenuity.

Mission data usually gets presented as tables. I wanted these missions to feel like goodbyes, so every machine is told as a character, with real NASA imagery, a dark, quiet design and a “Light a luminary” moment where visitors honour them.

It matters because exploration isn’t only about arriving. It’s about what stays behind, and the people who remember it. And one mission was never in the brief, but I couldn’t leave it out: Voyager 1.
details:
What it does: Luminary is an immersive scroll-driven website that turns ten NASA missions (5 lunar, 5 Mars) into a story about abandonment, endurance and memory. Each chapter pairs a mission’s real history with NASA/JPL imagery, and the closing “Keepers of the Light” section lets visitors light a luminary for the machines that were left behind.

Special Mention: Voyager 1. This wasn’t part of the challenge, but it has a special place in all our hearts, so I gave it its own chapter. Launched on September 5, 1977, Voyager 1 is still sending data home from the farthest distance any human-made object has ever travelled, using a transmitter about as powerful as a fridge light.

Impact: To make space history emotional and memorable for people who would never open a data table, and to remind visitors that these missions are still part of us.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, SVG, Google Fonts (Cormorant Garamond, Inter, IBM Plex Mono), and public NASA imagery via Wikimedia Commons.

Creativity: Instead of a mission catalogue, I used narrative, restraint and silence, with the design doing the emotional work.
